title: Cloudflare Adds Optional OAuth Scopes, Letting Developers Mark What Users May Decline
gist: Cloudflare added optional OAuth scopes so users can deselect individual permissions on the consent screen, with MCP servers named as the motivating case: agents request the union of everything they might ever do, forcing users to approve it all at once. Cloudflare reports over a million authorizations across thousands of third-party OAuth apps created since June, and says roles will expand to nearly every product in coming weeks.

themes.theme: Agent consent is a distinct product problem

insights.claim: Agent integrations break the consent model because an MCP server requests a broad permission set covering everything an agent could theoretically do, exposing the union of all possible actions on a single approve-or-deny screen.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Consent-screen friction is a concrete adoption tax on agent integrations — vendors that solve it convert more installs.
insights.quote: an MCP server might request a broad set of permissions because in theory an agent could use all of them, while most users would not want an agent to have that much access
insights.locator: The problem it targets is specific to agents

insights.claim: The mismatch is concrete and easy to enumerate: an agent that reads inventory to compare products does not need permission to change prices, one that checks order status does not need refund authority, and one that reads supplier records does not need payment access.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Read/write separation per agent task is the natural scope-design axis; use it to audit any agent integration's permission request.
insights.locator: That gap is easy to see in practice

insights.claim: Developers integrating agents face a lose-lose choice: request minimal permissions and break advanced use cases, or request everything and watch users abandon the consent screen.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Consent-screen abandonment is an under-measured funnel loss for agent products; granular consent is a conversion lever, not just a security feature.
insights.quote: That leaves developers with two bad choices: request minimal permissions and break advanced use cases, or request everything and watch users bounce from the consent screen.

insights.claim: Client owners can now mark scopes as optional using an optional_scopes array alongside the existing scopes list, letting users deselect individual permissions on the consent screen instead of approving or denying an application's full request.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A concrete configuration primitive competitors will be pressured to match in their OAuth surfaces.
insights.locator: Client owners can now mark scopes as optional

insights.claim: Required and optional scopes are evaluated against the scopes requested in a specific authorization flow rather than everything configured on the client, so a client configured with four scopes but requesting two shows the user only those two.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Per-flow scope evaluation lets one client offer progressively narrower consent by context — a design pattern for reducing install friction.

insights.claim: Clients that do not opt in keep their current behavior and the consent screen still grants the full requested set by default, making the change backward compatible.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Opt-in defaults mean adoption will lag availability — the security benefit only materializes if developers actively configure it.

insights.claim: Before this change, Cloudflare OAuth was all-or-nothing at consent time, and developers wanting finer control had to build a custom scope-selection screen ahead of the consent flow.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Platform-native granularity removes a category of custom developer work — a small but real reduction in integration cost.
insights.locator: Until now, Cloudflare OAuth handled that

insights.claim: Partial consent is not new: GitHub already lets users edit scopes and grant less than requested, Google shows granular checkboxes for non-sign-in scopes, and Microsoft Entra supports incremental consent with granted scopes appearing in the token's scp claim.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Granular consent is converging into a table-stakes identity-platform feature rather than a differentiator.

insights.claim: The distinguishing addition is developer control over which permissions may be dropped: marking a scope required means a user narrowing a request cannot remove something the application genuinely needs, which is materially different from hoping they do not.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The required/optional split is what makes granular consent shippable for real products — evaluate competing implementations on whether they offer it.
insights.quote: which is a different proposition from hoping they do not
insights.locator: What Cloudflare adds is developer control

insights.claim: None of this required changing OAuth itself — RFC 6749 already permits an authorization server to issue a token with narrower scope than requested; what changed is that providers are surfacing that latitude in the consent interface as agent integrations make broad requests routine.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Agent adoption is forcing providers to exercise long-dormant protocol latitude — expect similar dusting-off of existing standards rather than new ones.
insights.quote: None of this required changing OAuth. RFC 6749 already permits an authorization server to issue a token with a narrower scope than requested.
insights.locator: None of this required changing OAuth

insights.claim: Consent granularity is one of three parallel moves on agent authorization, alongside the MCP 2026-07-28 specification tightening client authorization by preferring pre-registered clients and Client ID Metadata Documents while deprecating Dynamic Client Registration.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Three-axis framing — who the agent is, which clients may connect, how much a user hands over — is a useful map for tracking agent-security product gaps.
insights.locator: The release joins a set of moves

insights.claim: Microsoft's hosted Azure DevOps MCP Server reached general availability without support for Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor because Entra lacks the client registration mechanisms those clients need.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Identity-layer gaps are already blocking major agent clients from enterprise MCP endpoints — a concrete drag on Microsoft's agent ecosystem reach.
insights.locator: The release joins a set of moves

insights.claim: When a user deselects an optional scope the access token carries only what was granted, so applications must inspect the scope parameter in the token response after exchanging the authorization code rather than assuming success means everything was granted.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Code written against the old all-or-nothing behavior will hit authorization errors on calls it expected to work — a silent breakage class in existing integrations.
insights.quote: Code written against the old behavior will meet authorization errors on calls it expected to work.
insights.locator: The developer consequence is an assumption

insights.claim: The recommended failure mode is to degrade rather than fail: an application losing a write scope should disable that feature and say so, instead of surfacing a 403 that a user reads as a broken integration.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Graceful degradation on partial consent is now a UX requirement — poor handling will show up as support load and churn.

insights.claim: The emerging agent design pattern is to require read access to whatever the agent queries, make write access optional, check the granted set before acting, and stop cleanly when authority is missing rather than improvising around it.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A read-required/write-optional default gives agents a materially better risk profile than demanding full write access at first contact — a reviewable standard for agent procurement.
insights.locator: For agents specifically, that shapes a design pattern

insights.claim: Cloudflare reports more than a million authorizations across thousands of third-party OAuth apps created since June, indicating rapid growth of its third-party integration surface.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A hard number on Cloudflare's developer-ecosystem traction — worth tracking quarter over quarter as a proxy for its platform pull.
insights.locator: Cloudflare reports more than a million authorizations

insights.claim: Cloudflare says it will expand account and zone-level roles to cover nearly every product over the coming weeks, adding API token roles, account membership options, and OAuth scopes.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Broad permission-model buildout is a prerequisite for enterprise agent deployments on Cloudflare — a near-term milestone to watch.
insights.locator: The company says it will expand account
